Set it in Entire settings under `strategy_options`:

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "strategy_options": {
    "checkpoints_v2": true,
    "full_transcript_generation_retention_days": 14
  }
}
```

Use `.entire/settings.json` for repo-wide settings, or `.entire/settings.local.json` for a local-only override. The value must be a positive integer number of days; missing/invalid/zero/negative values fall back to `60` days.

This retention only affects archived checkpoints v2 `/full/*` generations, and it is applied by:

```bash
entire clean --all          # preview
entire clean --all --force  # delete eligible archived generations
```

Relevant code: [settings.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go:794), [clean.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/clean.go:287), [cleanup.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/cleanup.go:343).

So the issue with `/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/entiredb` is that the checkpoints in `v2/full/0000000000023` are already older than 14 days but we're still keeping them. I think the bug is that after migration, we're keeping them around despite how old they are, even though the checkpoints themselves are 14+ days old, which is the default retention if I'm not mistaken. It should be checking the checkpoint time, not the time it was written to the filesystem

That diagnosis sounds right in shape: the cleanup path is meant to use `generation.json`, so I’m going to trace how migration populates `oldest/newest` there and compare it against the real `entiredb` ref. One small correction from the code I found earlier: the built-in fallback is 60 days, but `entiredb` may be overriding it to 14.

The `entiredb` archive confirms the bug: `v2/full/0000000000023:generation.json` says newest checkpoint is `2026-04-30T18:25:48Z`, and the archive commit itself is from today. That looks like migration/merge time leaking into retention metadata, not the original checkpoint creation time.

The smoking gun is in `computeGenerationTimestamps`: it explicitly uses `/full/current` commit history because `/full/*` trees don’t carry session metadata. That is fragile after migration because those commits are fresh even when the checkpoint metadata they represent is old. Next I’m checking whether `/main` can be used as the source of truth for checkpoint `created_at`, then I’ll patch the timestamp computation and tests.

I’m going to make the checkpoint creation time a first-class write option, preserve it during migration, and have generation rotation derive retention timestamps from `/main` metadata for the checkpoints actually present in `/full/current`. For already-bad archives where `/main` metadata is missing or wrong, I’ll keep a fallback path so cleanup can still reason from transcript event timestamps when that is the only durable source left.

Yep, you had the bug right: retention was effectively trusting generation write/commit time after migration, instead of the checkpoint’s original time.

I changed that in three places:

- [checkpoint.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint.go): added `CreatedAt` to `WriteCommittedOptions`.
- [migrate.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/migrate.go): migration now preserves the v1 checkpoint `created_at` when writing v2.
- [v2_generation.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/v2_generation.go) and [cleanup.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/cleanup.go): v2 generation retention now derives age from checkpoint metadata, falling back to transcript event timestamps for partial/older v2 data, and only then falling back to `generation.json`.

I also added regression coverage in [migrate_test.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/migrate_test.go), [v2_generation_test.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/v2_generation_test.go), and [clean_test.go](/Users/ninawork/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/clean_test.go).

One nuance: I checked `entiredb`, and it does not appear to set `full_transcript_generation_retention_days`; the code default is `60`, not `14`. Also, `v2/full/0000000000023` contains some transcript timestamps from `2026-04-30`, so whole-generation cleanup will still keep that ref until its newest checkpoint ages out. This patch fixes the age source; it does not yet split mixed-age generations into per-checkpoint pruning.

Verification:

- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint` passed
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli` passed

- full `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy -count=1` still fails on the existing `TestResolveAgentForRewind/dynamically_registered_agent_resolves_by_type` global registration issue; that same test passes in isolation.
The code default should be 14, not 60.
Good catch. I’ll switch the default to 14 and update the expectations that were documenting the old 60-day fallback, then rerun the small settings/cleanup checks plus lint.

why is this the case? ` Also, v2/full/0000000000023 contains some transcript timestamps from 2026-04-30`

Because `v2/full/0000000000023` is a storage generation, not a time bucket.

A `v2/full/*` generation contains whatever raw transcript checkpoint trees happened to be in `/full/current` when rotation happened. Rotation is count-based, not age-based, so a generation can mix:

- migrated old checkpoints, with transcript events from months ago
- newly-created checkpoints, with transcript events from April 30
- possibly merged-in local `/full/current` data during v2 push conflict recovery

In `entiredb`, I found at least one real recent checkpoint inside that archive: `09/d2e902cdc5`. Its v2 main metadata had `created_at: 2026-04-30T04:38:05Z`, and its raw transcript in `v2/full/0000000000023` also had April 30 transcript event timestamps. So that archive is mixed: some old checkpoint transcripts plus at least one actually-recent checkpoint.

That means whole-generation cleanup cannot delete `0000000000023` yet without also deleting the recent checkpoint’s raw transcript. The patch fixes “what age do we measure?” but cleanup is still generation-granular. If we want old checkpoints inside a mixed generation to disappear sooner, we need a second feature: rewrite/prune archived generation trees per checkpoint, not just delete entire `v2/full/<generation>` refs.

Because `23` is just the archived generation counter, not a date or retention bucket.

In this repo, `/full/current` rotates when it reaches `100` checkpoint directories. The archive code picks `max(existing archived generation) + 1`, so `0000000000023` means “the next archive after `22` existed at rotation time.” Older archive refs may have since been cleaned up, not fetched locally, or moved around by remote sync, which is why you can now see only `23` and `current`.

For this specific ref:

- `0000000000023` was originally created by a normal `Archive generation` commit at `2026-04-28 17:27:46 -0700`.
- At that point it had exactly `100` checkpoint raw transcripts.
- It later got updated by `Merge local checkpoints into archived generation` on `2026-04-30 11:26:05 -0700`.
- That merge path is push/rotation conflict recovery: remote had already rotated `/full/current`, so the local `/full/current` data was merged into the latest remote archive, which happened to be `23`.
- It now has `119` checkpoint raw transcripts; `/full/current` has `12`.

So the “why all the way in 23?” answer is: migration and/or early v2 writes filled `/full/current` in batches of 100, advancing the counter quickly, and then push recovery merged newer local checkpoints into the latest archive rather than creating a new time-based bucket.
